questions.q: Describe the different types of markets and how they differ.
answer: We buy goods and services from many kinds of markets, which differ in cost and convenience.

answer.text: Held on a fixed day of the week, they have no permanent shops, so costs are low and goods are cheaper and open to bargaining.
Permanent shops close to home are convenient, familiar, and often sell on credit.
These house many shops selling branded goods and are usually more expensive.
People can now buy from home, with goods delivered to them. Some markets sell directly to consumers (retail) and others in bulk to shopkeepers (wholesale).

questions.q: Explain the chain of markets from producer to consumer.
answer: Most goods pass through a chain of markets before they reach us.

answer.text: A wholesaler buys goods in large quantities directly from producers and sells them to retailers. Buying in bulk allows the wholesaler to get lower prices.
A retailer buys smaller quantities from the wholesaler and sells them to the final consumer in the shop or market.
So the usual chain runs from the producer to the wholesaler, then to the retailer, and finally to the consumer, with the price rising at each step.
The gains are shared unequally along this chain — big traders often profit more than the producer or the small seller.
